items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed fleet-wide and blocked for public exposure or security-sensitive releases. Fleet-doctor has no run or results; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps are unavailable. Authentication boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are unverified. TLS evidence only shows no certificates expiring within 30 days and does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is a technical baseline, not certification: 37 pass, 16 fail, 6 unknown. Risk severity is high for public launch and medium for bounded reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Retain private launch gates; continue only authorized read-only evidence work.

Exact decision: keep SearchWoot private and preview-only. Public exposure, security-sensitive release, alert expansion, deployment, configuration or credential changes, dependency additions, and external outreach remain blocked until access, secrets, isolation, release, TLS, dependency, monitoring, incident, disclosure, rights, privacy, accuracy, attribution, measurement, and owner evidence is complete. Ordinary reversible growth may continue only within existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, claims, and provenance boundaries.

Use authorized metadata and retained artifacts only to attach dated, redacted evidence or explicit unknowns for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Do not access credentials or private containers, change permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue, exploit targets, or conduct outreach.

items.title: Maintain evidence-needed fleet security disposition and private launch gates

Permit ordinary reversible growth only when it introduces no credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, or cross-site behavior and preserves existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, and data-handling boundaries.
